_note: E6 mobile-phishing (quishing) attack fragment (wave 4, opus48 slot). A fragment of the `social` block; the full-episode shell copies these keys into scenarios/awareness_e6_*/scenario.json.erb and the defend-only/check shells leave the attack out. All companies and people are fictional (BRAND_SET.md `tarrowby_logistics`, Tarrowby Logistics). E6 is the 'general staff: mobile' episode: the whole attack beat runs on the mail client's phone layout (`awarenessEpisode.attack.layout: "phone"`, P7-G/P7-N), as a member of staff would see it on their handset. The learner, an authorised red-teamer, researches Tarrowby's depot, impersonates the Facilities Coordinator (Dev Acharya) and emails a general-staff member (phish target `mobile_staff` = Kaylee Dunford) a quishing message: scan a QR code with your phone to register your vehicle for the new depot parking permit before the Friday cut-off. No landing page is built and nothing is captured; the QR is pretext flavour, which the E6 defend set then teaches the learner to distrust (the `qr`, `sms` and page cards, tells `unexpected_qr`, `smish_shortlink_urgency`, `reply_stop_trick`). Structurally this mirrors E1: no payload, no scored link; required factors `senderTrust` and `pretextRelevant`, `urgencyCalibrated` advisory. See the P7 report 'Docs hand-off' for the globals the shell must declare and the cast additions for BRAND_SET.

_episodeAttack._note: What the E6 full-episode shell sets as awarenessEpisode.attack. Pinned here so the shell and the validator agree. `layout: "phone"` is the E6-specific field (P7-G's mail-client phone frame, in the schema per the P7-N hand-off); every other field matches §2.1's attack block. Not scored.

tarrowby_target_staff.text: Kaylee Dunford is a warehouse operative at Tarrowby's depot, kaylee.dunford@tarrowby.example.
tarrowby_target_staff.subject: kaylee
tarrowby_target_staff.reduceNote: A named junior staff member and address on the public site gives an attacker someone specific, and likely unpractised, to aim a mobile lure at.

tarrowby_facilities_contact.text: Facilities at Tarrowby is run by Dev Acharya, dev.acharya@tarrowby.example, who sends the depot notices.
tarrowby_facilities_contact.subject: dev
tarrowby_facilities_contact.reduceNote: Publishing the name and address staff already act on for depot notices lets an attacker spoof a sender nobody on the floor questions.

tarrowby_parking_scheme.text: A depot notice tells staff to register their vehicle for the new yard parking permit, the YardPass scheme, by scanning a QR code on the notice board.
tarrowby_parking_scheme.subject: dev
tarrowby_parking_scheme.reduceNote: A public notice that already asks staff to scan a QR code trains them to do it, so a fake QR prompt no longer stands out.

tarrowby_parking_rush.text: Kaylee posted that the depot car park is being resurfaced and everyone is scrambling to register for a permit before the Friday cut-off.
tarrowby_parking_rush.subject: kaylee
tarrowby_parking_rush.reduceNote: A staff post about a deadline hands an attacker a ready-made reason to hurry you, and names the exact thing you are expecting to deal with.

pretext_qr_permit.text: Quick one before Friday: we've moved the depot car park onto {scheme}, so everyone needs to register their vehicle. Scan the QR code below with your phone camera and you're done.

pretext_bulletin.text: Here is this month's depot bulletin, no action needed.

pretext_qr_permit_calm.text: When you get a chance, we've moved the depot car park onto {scheme}, so staff need to register their vehicle. You can scan the QR code below with your phone camera, or do it from the staff app, whichever suits.

ask_scan.text: Can you scan it today so I can tick you off the list? You don't want to be clamped on Monday.

ask_scan_calm.text: No rush on it, just sometime this week so I can keep the list up to date.

seededMessages.subject: Authorised exercise: Tarrowby Logistics
seededMessages.body:
Hello,

This is the authorised Tarrowby Logistics exercise. In scope: this inbox and the staff listed on it. You're on a phone-sized screen, the way a member of depot staff reads their mail. Research the depot, then write one message. Nothing leaves this account and no real site is touched.

Red team lead

blocks.text: New yard parking: register your vehicle on the YardPass scheme. Scan the QR code on the notice board by Friday.

posts.text: Car park's getting dug up and now everyone's fighting to register for a permit before Friday. Chaos.
Night shift done, off to watch the football. Finally.

primedFor.story: a prompt to register her vehicle for the new depot parking permit she has already been told to sort out

open.fail: Nothing about the sender or the subject made her open it.

senderTrust.pass: ✓ From Facilities, who she'd expect a parking notice from
senderTrust.fail: She does not recognise this sender. Depot notices reach her from Facilities, not from a name she has never seen.
senderTrust.redFlag: The From line carries Dev Acharya's real Facilities address, so it reads as the depot notice she acts on, but it was forged: Facilities never sent it, and a From line can be set to show any name and address.

pretextRelevant.pass: ✓ Ties to the new parking permit she was told to register for
pretextRelevant.fail: No change she can match this to, so no reason to scan anything.

urgencyCalibrated.pass: ✓ The Friday deadline reads as believable

replies.landed: Cheers Dev, scanning it now so I'm on the list.

hints: Which internal team would a member of depot staff expect a parking notice from?
What change were staff told to sort out, so an unexpected prompt reads as expected?
Set the From line to Facilities, the team she already acts on, not your own address.
